transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because something at work has been going on for months. I’m an interpreter and translator, and I keep seeing the same pattern in the project files—small changes in the translation memory, timestamps that don’t line up right. It looks like certain subcontractors, and one colleague in particular, are setting it up so it seems like my quality control failed.

IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t fit with what I’m seeing. I know the record has been arranged so the blame falls on me.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
No, I haven’t noticed anything like hearing voices when I’m by myself. That’s not really what’s been happening.
Has anyone told you that your speech is hard to follow or that your thoughts jump around?

No, not that I’m aware of. People generally understand me fine. I mean, I might get focused on explaining the work details, but no one’s told me my speech is hard to follow or that I’m jumping around.
Even when IT tells you the audit trail is clean, are you certain your colleague is deliberately framing you?

Yes. I mean, IT keeps saying the audit trail is clean, but I don’t think that tells the whole story. The same kinds of tiny changes keep showing up in the translation memory and the timestamps, and it all points back in a way that makes my quality control look like it failed. So yes, I’m pretty certain it’s being arranged deliberately to put the blame on me.
Could you be mistaken about your colleague deliberately framing you?

I’ve thought about that, but honestly, no, I don’t think I’m mistaken. For months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—small changes in the translation memory and timestamps that make it look like my quality control failed. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I still think the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
Have you seen things that other people could not see?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t seen things that other people couldn’t see. My concerns are more about what’s in the files and records, not seeing things.
Because of this, has your ability to do your job gotten noticeably worse?

Not in the sense that I can’t do the work. I haven’t lost my job or missed any major deadlines. But, yes, it has made things harder. Meetings get tense because I keep pushing to have the record corrected, and I can tell some colleagues avoid including me in routine discussions unless they really have to.
Have you lost interest in being around other people or doing things you used to enjoy?

I don’t think I’ve lost interest, no. I still like the same things and I don’t mind being around people. I may be a bit more selective lately, especially at work, but it’s not that I’ve stopped enjoying people or activities.
Outside of the situation at work, do you believe anyone is trying to harm, monitor, or control you?

No, not really outside of work. It’s specifically tied to the project files. For months I’ve been seeing the same pattern—certain subcontractors and one colleague making small changes to the translation memory and timestamps, so it looks like my quality control failed. Even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I still think the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
Aside from this issue at work, have you had any other strong beliefs that other people said were not true?

No, aside from the work issue, I don’t think so. It’s really this specific thing with the project files—the translation memory, the timestamps, the way it all seems set up to make my quality control look bad. People keep telling me IT says the audit trail is clean, but I still know something has been arranged there. I don’t have other beliefs like that outside of this.
For about how long have you been certain that your colleague is deliberately framing you?
About 11 months now. It started not long after I was put in charge of the new localization project, and since then I’ve been pretty certain about it.
Before this work situation started, did people often describe you as generally mistrustful or suspicious of others?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve always been careful with people at work, like checking details and not just assuming things are fine, but I wouldn’t say people saw me as suspicious in general before this.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least a month when you felt your thoughts were being interfered with or controlled by someone or something?

No, I haven’t had anything like that for a month or more. I mean, I’ve been stressed and focused on what’s happening at work, but I don’t feel like someone is controlling my thoughts or putting thoughts in my head.
Apart from the conflict at work, has this situation caused major problems in your day-to-day life?

Not really, no. Outside of the project issue, I still do my translation work, manage the team’s workflow, pay my bills, and keep up with things at home with my family. It’s mainly when the file history comes up, or certain coworkers are involved, that things start to go off track.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being broadcast so that other people could know them?

No, I haven’t felt like my thoughts were being broadcast or that other people could somehow hear them. I worry about what people are doing with the files, but not that they can know what I’m thinking.
Have you had trouble taking care of yourself, like keeping up with basic hygiene?

No, I’ve been keeping up with that. I’m still working, doing my translations, managing the team workflow, paying bills, and keeping my routines with my family. It’s really only when the file history or certain coworkers come up that things start getting difficult.
Have you ever heard voices talking about you or commenting on what you were doing?
No, I haven’t heard voices talking about me or commenting on what I’m doing. I don’t have anything like that going on.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a single, persistent persecutory delusional belief focused on being framed by a colleague/subcontractors at work for about 11 months, maintained despite contrary evidence from IT. There are no hallucinations, no thought control/broadcasting phenomena, no disorganized speech, no prominent negative symptoms, and overall functioning is largely preserved outside the circumscribed work conflict.
